stemMd: “All successful local shops have websites. Therefore creating a website will make any local shop successful.” What is the flaw?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It denies that any successful shop has a website.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It compares no shops at all.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It proves that websites are useless.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It confuses a website with a physical address.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It treats a feature associated with success as sufficient to cause success.

explanationMd: The premise says success is accompanied by a website. It does not show that adding a website guarantees success; other conditions may matter, and success may enable investment in a site. The conclusion reverses and causalizes the association.

distractorRationale.a: The premise explicitly affirms that association.
distractorRationale.b: The statement concerns successful local shops.
distractorRationale.c: The flaw does not show websites have no value.
distractorRationale.d: The issue is necessity versus sufficiency and causation.
